title: Controls drawn into pictures over buttons, a file input, a treegrid, switches and ranges
blurb: Five controls from the ui-feed collection that live inside a picture, rebuilt around native elements: waypoint buttons and a tooltip on a hand-drawn map, a file input on a scrapbook page, a treegrid of a night's backup on a green screen, a hob's child lock and a crop box on a cutting mat.
question: How much of a control's picture can the canvas paint itself, with the native elements only where something is pressed, typed or read out?
result: Most of each picture was painted once by the canvas, with buttons, a tooltip, a file input, a treegrid, two switches in front of a disabled fieldset and four ranges drawn only where they are used. All five took taps and drags on an emulated phone and stopped painting at rest. Nothing here is verified on a phone.
